title: Successor summed-counter invariant
statement: Let $A$ be counting-sort arguments, let $kf$ assign a natural-number key to each item index, and let $r$ be a natural number. Suppose an integer-valued memory map $mu'$ has, for every $t\le r$, the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)<t$ at address $A.cnt+t$, and, for every $t<A.nb$ with $r\le t$, the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)=t$ at address $A.cnt+(t+1)$. After replacing the value at address $A.cnt+(r+1)$ by the number of indices $i<A.n$ with $kf(i)<r+1$, these two counter conditions hold at stage $r+1$.
hypotheses_covered: The summed-counter conditions hold at stage $r$: for all $t\le r$, address $A.cnt+t$ stores the count of keys below $t$; for all $t<A.nb$ with $r\le t$, address $A.cnt+(t+1)$ stores the count of keys equal to $t$.
